text:
Maria: we just saw a strange tail-latency spike on the awq-int8 model when coalescer is enabled, looks tied to prefix cache hits + batching
Kevin: ugh, seen that before in a slightly different form. can you paste the traces?
Maria: putting the minimal logs below — observed on dedicated pool during a small traffic replay
Maria: ```
req id=abc123 model=awq-13b quant=int8 coalescer=on batch_size=8 prefix_hit=true latency_ms=420
req id=abc124 model=awq-13b quant=int8 coalescer=on batch_size=8 prefix_hit=false latency_ms=45
```
Priya: those numbers are wild. prefix_hit=true should be faster. maybe coalescer is stalling when it tries to merge requests with cached KV states
Jamie: can you repro with coalescer=off and coalescer=max_coalesce=1? that will tell if the merge step is the culprit
Maria: repro script: `./tools/replay -t small -q awq-13b -c on` — will run both variants now and post perf-bot output
perf-bot: summary: coalescer=on p95=210ms p99=420ms; coalescer=off p95=48ms p99=92ms; memory spikes observed at coalescer=on
Kevin: memory spikes + prefix cache = potential KV cache eviction thrash. when coalescer aggregates, it may reuse incorrect KV references for different prompt prefixes if we don't snapshot offsets
Alex: could also be a quant-specific decoder path: AWQ int8 uses a fused kernel that assumes contiguous KV buffers. coalescer's scatter/gather might be copying incorrectly and causing extra memcpys behind the scenes
Priya: good call. @Alex, can you check the kernel codepaths for fused-atten on the awq runtime? specifically look for in-place ops when prefix_len>0
Alex: will grep now. quick note: on fp8 experiments we didn't see this because the runtime uses a different layout (tile-based), so that explains model-variant differences
Maria: test matrix I'm running: coalescer on/off, batch_size 1/4/8, prefix_hit true/false, quant awq-int8 vs fp8 vs gptq-8bit
Jamie: flag suggestion: add a conservative snapshot flag to coalescer: `--coalescer-snapshot-kv` which forces copies instead of references when prefix_len>0. cheap to toggle for canary
Maria: local test of snapshot flag reduced p99 from 420->95 but added ~6% token CPU cost
Kevin: 6% CPU is acceptable if it prevents tail spikes and correctness issues. more concerning is accuracy delta — any quality regression with snapshot on?
Maria: ran 150 eval prompts comparing awq-int8 coalescer=on (snapshot) vs coalescer=off — BLEU-ish style metric showed no meaningful delta (within noise). diffs were mostly formatting tokens
Priya: sounds like a viable mitigation. still want to root cause the memory thrash. can you capture jemalloc stats and slab histo during a failing run?
Maria: saving jemalloc heap profiles now, will upload to #eng-ml-artifacts when done
perf-bot: artifact uploaded: s3://redwood-artifacts/1954321000/heap-profile.tgz
Jamie: next steps: 1) ship `--coalescer-snapshot-kv` as a canary on staging dedicated pool; 2) Alex to audit fused kernel paths for in-place ops; 3) Priya/Kevin to run longer evals for accuracy drift across quant variants
Alex: quick FYI — if kernel audit finds in-place ops, we can land a micro-patch that avoids mutating kv buffers when coalescer is on
Kevin: if we opt for snapshot flag, add telemetry: counter for snapshot hits and bytes copied, and a tag for prefix_hit vs miss
Maria: noted. I'll open the RFC + PR: RFC-3787 coalescer snapshot and PR #8124. assigning followups in the thread. thanks all :thumbsup:
infra-bot: deploy-plan created for staging canary with flag `--coalescer-snapshot-kv=true` (plan id dp-8342)
Maria: logging this as postmortem-lite so we can reference for future quant onboarding docs
